## Clustering

### Generating a simulated dataset

Let us generate a small dataset, of 15 samples (columns) and 20 "genes" (rows):
We will generate this dataset such that there are 3 groups:

```{r}
set.seed(123)

## this are 3 seed "patients"
p1 = c(rnorm(10),rnorm(10,mean=1))
p2 = c(rnorm(10,mean=2),rnorm(10))
p3 = c(rnorm(10,mean=-1),rnorm(10))

plot(p1,type='b',col='green',main='Seed patients',ylim=c(-3,5))
lines(p2,type='b',col='red')
lines(p3,type='b',col='blue')

```



```{r}
## now we add fluctuations around the values of this patient
## to create the first group of 5 patients

s = 1

X1 = sapply(1:5,function(i) {
  x = rnorm(20,sd=s)
  p = p1 + x
  return(p)
})

## now we add fluctuations around the values of this patient
## to create the second group of 5 patients
X2 = sapply(1:5,function(i) {
  x = rnorm(20,sd=s) ## we add fluctuations with a mean of 0
  p = p2 + x
  return(p)
})

X3 = sapply(1:5,function(i) {
  x = rnorm(20,sd=s) ## we add fluctuations with a mean of 0
  p = p3 + x
  return(p)
})

X = cbind(X1,X2,X3)
colnames(X) = paste0('Pat.',1:ncol(X))
rownames(X) = paste0('Gene_',1:nrow(X))


##
boxplot(X)
```


### Displaying the dataset as a heatmap

```{r}
#library(pheatmap)
pheatmap::pheatmap(X,
         cluster_cols = TRUE,
         cluster_rows = FALSE, 
         clustering_distance_cols = 'euclidean',
         clustering_method = 'complete')


pheatmap::pheatmap(X,
         cluster_cols = TRUE,
         cluster_rows = FALSE, 
         clustering_distance_cols = 'euclidean',
         clustering_method = 'single')
```

We see the three groups appearing clearly!

Kmeans:

```{r}
## beware that we need to transpose X if we want to cluster the patients!!
km = kmeans(t(X),centers=3)
clust = data.frame(Cluster = as.factor(km$cluster))
clust
```


We can cut the tree

```{r}
hm = pheatmap::pheatmap(X,
         cluster_cols = TRUE,
         cluster_rows = TRUE, 
         clustering_distance_cols = 'minkowski',
         clustering_method = 'ward.D2',
         annotation_col = clust)
```

Optimal number of clusters?

```{r}
# Silhouette and WSS plot
library(factoextra)
fviz_nbclust(t(X), kmeans, method = "silhouette")
fviz_nbclust(t(X), kmeans, method = "wss")
```


```{r}
height = 10
hcol = as.dendrogram(hm$tree_col)
plot(hcol);abline(h=height,lty=3,col='red',lwd=2)
```

```{r}
cutree(hm$tree_col,h=10)
```



## Look at the distance matrix

```{r}
dd = dist(t(X))
h = hclust(dd)
dd
h
```




## Principal Component Analysis

```{r}
pca = prcomp(t(X))
```

```{r}
variance = (pca$sdev)^2
barplot(variance)
```

```{r}
prop.var = variance/sum(variance)
barplot(prop.var,names.arg = paste0('PC',1:length(variance)))
```



```{r}
pca$x
```




```{r}
rot = pca$rotation
par(las=2,cex=0.8,mar=c(2,5,2,2),mfrow=c(1,2))
barplot(rot[,1],horiz=TRUE,main='PC1')
barplot(rot[,2],horiz=TRUE,main='PC2')

```


```{r}
new.coordinates = pca$x
color = c(rep('green',5),rep('red',5),rep('blue',5))

plot(new.coordinates[,1],new.coordinates[,2],pch=19,
     xlab='PC1',ylab='PC2',col=color)

#plot(X[1,],X[2,],pch=19,
#     xlab='Gene_1',ylab='Gene_2',col=color)

```


Other dataset: decathlon

```{r}
library(factoextra)
data(decathlon2)
decathlon2.active = decathlon2[, 1:10]
```


How are the variables distributed?


```{r}
par(mar=c(5,4,4,4))
boxplot(decathlon2.active,las=2)
```
Scales are very different! They need to be scaled before running the PCA:


```{r}
deca.scaled = scale(decathlon2.active)
par(mar=c(5,4,4,4))
boxplot(deca.scaled,las=2)
```


```{r}
decathlon2.active = decathlon2[,1:10]
res.pca.nosc = prcomp(decathlon2.active, scale = FALSE)
res.pca.sc = prcomp(decathlon2.active, scale = TRUE)
```

```{r}
variance = res.pca.sc$sdev^2
prop.var = variance/sum(variance)
m.var = mean(prop.var)
names(prop.var) = paste0('PC',1:length(prop.var))
barplot(cumsum(prop.var),cex.names = 0.7);abline(h=0.7,lwd=2,lty=3)
```


```{r}
barplot(prop.var,cex.names = 0.6);abline(h=m.var,lwd=2,lty=3)
```


```{r}
library(factoextra)
fviz_pca_ind(res.pca.sc,axes = c(1,2))
```
```{r}
rot = res.pca.sc$rotation
par(las=2,cex=0.8,mar=c(4,5,2,2),mfrow=c(1,2))
barplot(rot[,1],horiz=TRUE,main='PC1')
barplot(rot[,2],horiz=TRUE,main='PC2')
```

```{r}
fviz_pca_biplot(res.pca.sc)
```

We can add additional information from external variables; for example, at which competition was this performance achieved?

```{r}
competition = as.factor(decathlon2$Competition)
```

```{r}
fviz_pca_ind(res.pca.sc,col.ind = competition)
```


What happens if we transpose the matrix??

```{r}
Y = scale(decathlon2.active)
Y = t(Y)
res.pca2 = prcomp(Y, scale = TRUE)
```

```{r}
fviz_pca_ind(res.pca2,axes = c(1,2))
```
